t: What Negative Results Archive Is All About
title: What Negative Results Archive Is All About
description: Most experiments fail, but journals publish successes — the file-drawer problem. Null results are knowledge: knowing a drug does nothing, a material doesn't superconduct, or an effect doesn't replicate saves the next lab years. Michelson-Morley (1887) is history's most famous null result: no aether drift, and physics had to be rebuilt. This database is the complete negative result: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.
definition: Negative Results Archive: a complete reference database of full negative result records.
key_points: What this database holds: full negative result records, each with definition, key facts, and a runnable demo program.
Scope: Most experiments fail, but journals publish successes — the file-drawer problem.
Every record is the full entry — never a stub or description alone.
Teaching ladder: Foundations first, then Compounded, then Advanced.

t: Core Vocabulary of Negative Results Archive
title: Core Vocabulary of Negative Results Archive
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Negative Results Archive — learn them first and every later record reads faster: null result: experiment finding no effect within its detection power; file-drawer problem: unpublished negatives biasing the literature; publication bias: systematic over-publishing of positive results; power: probability an experiment detects a real effect of a given size.
definition: The working vocabulary of Negative Results Archive: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: null result: experiment finding no effect within its detection power
file-drawer problem: unpublished negatives biasing the literature
publication bias: systematic over-publishing of positive results
power: probability an experiment detects a real effect of a given size
pre-registration: logging the plan before data collection
replication: independent repeat testing the same claim
how_it_works: Read each term and definition twice.
Use three terms in a sentence of your own.
Quiz yourself with the demo program.
Add new terms as you meet them.
